name: Lamington
origin: Named for Lord Lamington, Governor of Queensland from 1896 to 1901; squares of sponge cake dipped in a thin chocolate icing and rolled in desiccated coconut, said to have been invented by his household's cook to use up day-old sponge.

process.name: cream butter and sugar
process.description: beat butter and sugar until light

process.name: fold in flour
process.description: fold in flour, leavening and salt

process.name: bake
process.description: bake in a sheet pan, cool, then cut into squares

notes: A standard light butter-cake sponge (between a Victoria sponge and a genoise in richness), matching lamington's real role as a practical way to use up plain sponge. Tagged 'tunnel' oven family: lamington sheet sponge is a standardised, high-volume product commonly produced on a continuous belt line in commercial bakeries, unlike a single-pan home-style cake. The chocolate icing dip and desiccated-coconut coating are separately-prepared components applied after baking, out of scope for this batter's formulation.
